title: Don't keep all eggs together
summary: Spreading money across different kinds of things means one bad result hurts less.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Meera's family has ₹10,000 of virtual play money for a school fair stall. Her cousin says, "Put it all into one thing, mangoes!" Then a hailstorm spoils the mango crop and the whole stall is empty.

**Diversification** means spreading money across different things, so one bad result does not sink everything. Meera splits it: ₹4,000 on mangoes, ₹3,000 on lemonade and ₹3,000 on paper fans. If mangoes fail, lemonade and fans may still sell.

The things should be **different baskets**. Three kinds of mangoes all fall to the same hailstorm, so that is not much spreading.

Diversification **reduces risk, but it does not remove it**, and it does not promise a profit. Any growth figure in an example is an assumption for this example, not a promise.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

options.text: So she is guaranteed a profit
